title: Remembering Artists From Another Time: Ellsworth Kelly
author: Richard Schulman
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/0-1.jpeg-680x461.webp)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/07/remembering-
artists-from-another-time-ellsworth-kelly/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/0-1.jpeg-680x461.webp)

Ellsworth Kelly, artist.

**Truthful Fictions**

The camera cannot miss the words that are destined to arrive. Intoxicated by a
hint of the fantastical,

and the voices of seminal artists, I placed my camera in a space of time. I
discovered the demands of connecting dates and places within a revolution of
continuous art history. How remiss would the camera have been to not advance,
frame after frame, like a reconnaissance sniper in the naked woods.

My camera hears secrets. Thousands have posed before and will after this day.

Artists of various generations have been influenced by many; in a similar
manner, many have been influenced by those generations. I was never
photographing just one person. I was attempting to photograph every voice
associated with the entire DNA of modern art in a single frame.

It was like a witch’s brew—a promise that night will follow day, and the
morning will become night. When I visit the studios of most artists I am
invariably invited to see more than I previously knew.

The artist  _Ellsworth Kelly_ welcomed me into his home, then, with great
care, took me by the arm. He turned me around and we walked the land like two
characters out of Rølvaag’s  _Giants in the Earth._

The artists’ hands pointed the way, and touched the wind. I followed this aged
man ageless stroller across his grounds, and property in silence. He shared a
few words before we paused in our reflections…

For a brief glimpse over the artist’s shoulder I saw two men in a mirror (the
shape of his works,) the artist, and the man with the camera. I knew we would
make a visual memory with the mere shutter heard.

Entering his house and studio reminds me of a visual marriage between the
movie  _Ex Machina_ with

Nathaniel Hawthorne’s tome “ _The House of the Seven Gables_ ”. It was like an
exploration of minimalist darkness— eerie and alone, with sounds and ideas
lurking behind corners. I was not scared, but a bit frightened of the unknown.

Kelly the artist was like a single thread amidst the tapestry of art history.
His work has become part of the fabric of contemporary art history. If you
stare long enough into his canvases you will see the life of a planet; your
dreams can carry you wherever you need them to be. You might meet head-on the
way we decipher the history of who we are. His vibrant geometrical shapes,
spoke to you if you listened.

![](https://images.squarespace-
cdn.com/content/v1/5877d74f725e2540a2f2c4d7/25d4164c-7a87-4934-b912-ca3d4ba6d62f/0.jpeg)

He was a mere strand among the finest materials of cloth; woven into the
artist’s world.

I realized that after three sessions with Kelly, he and I have changed, and my
cameras have changed. What we talk about will be different. In the the spirit
of discovery, I have seen the artists’ work in Tokyo, Berlin and countless
other cities. The moment is singularly different and the verve felt here is
powerful. Red, blue, yellow and other colors hang like drapery offering
protection and invitation to imagine.

I remember Emily Pulitzer describing a perfect storm: Ellsworth Kelly and
Richard Serra lured Tadao Ando for a meeting of tremendous minds. It was the
timelessness of artistic fervor felt in a single frame. I realized my camera
had framed each of these people and their works.The story about the
conversation that took place to convince Tadao Ando to create the Pulitzer
Foundation was like feeling one million fireflies enter any part of the insane
brain that is mine. Seeing the entire scope of three giants in one room and
Serra and Kelly committing to contribute, was simply inspiring. It was a
beautiful story. Three heads of creative prowess together, imagined as I peer
into my archives reliving the moments as if I was among them.

Each time I photographed Kelly and waved thank you for the time he shared with
me,I envisioned a scenario of death. Each memory of my portrait sessions,
would be a lasting finale. Yet, more was to follow. Fantastical dreams
prevailed again and again.
